## Scope

The agency's two cloud voice platforms — the N8NN citizen contact center on
Amazon Connect (AWS commercial `.com`, by authorized exception) and internal
telephony on Microsoft Teams Phone in GCC Moderate — share identical network
requirements (<75 ms one-way, <30 ms jitter, <1% loss, DSCP EF). One
SD-WAN/AAN modernization investment therefore enables both; **voice is the
canary** that exposes network problems other applications hide.

## Learning objectives

- State the ITU-T G.114 150 ms one-way delay ceiling and derive the ~75 ms
  network budget after codec and jitter-buffer overhead.
- Map network conditions to MOS via the ITU-T G.107 E-model and defend the
  ≥4.0 MOS floor.
- Explain the Amazon Connect `.com` authorized exception, its SSP SA-9
  boundary documentation, and ATO-renewal maintenance obligations.
- Diagnose asymmetric routing as a stateful-firewall session killer and
  explain why SD-WAN overlay eliminates it structurally.
- Plan Teams Phone Direct Routing (SBC selection, FedRAMP-authorized cloud
  SBC) and E911 compliance under Kari's Law and Ray Baum's Act.
- Size DSCP EF capacity for hybrid agents (max concurrent hybrid agents ×
  200 Kbps).

## Key concepts

- MPLS hairpin vs. local breakout (DIA), with the Portland → Washington →
  AWS us-west-2 worked example.
- AWS `.us` vs. `.com` vs. GovCloud federal delivery models.
- WebRTC/RTP/SRTP requirements; DSCP EF (46) steering; FEC at ≥0.5% loss.
- Hybrid agent = two simultaneous DSCP EF streams (Connect + Teams Phone).
- "DIA enables; SASE achieves" — the pipe vs. the control stack.
- Direct Routing SBC options (on-prem vs. cloud) and E911 LIS/ELIN.

## Implementation sequence

1. Phase 1 (months 1–3): SD-WAN, local breakout, DSCP EF steering, FEC;
   measure and document G.114 compliance per location — **a hard gate
   before any migration**.
2. Phase 2 (months 2–5): Amazon Connect — exception confirmation, contact
   flows, Entra ID federation, pilot with MOS measurement, S3 recording
   pipeline validation.
3. Phase 3 (months 4–8): Teams Phone — SBC deployment, per-location E911
   testing, PBX number inventory, geographic porting tranches with parallel
   PBX operation.
4. Phase 4 (months 6+): continuous monitoring — MOS ≥4.0 SLA alerting,
   SIEM integration, ATO exception review, 20x KSI alignment.

## Compliance hooks

AC-4, SC-7, SC-8, SI-3, SI-4, AU-12, CA-7, SA-9, AU-9, SC-28, IA-8. Also
ITU-T G.114/G.107, RFC 3246/3550/4594, TIC 3.0 Use Case E, OMB M-22-09,
CISA ZTMM v2.0, Kari's Law and Ray Baum's Act (47 CFR Part 9), Privacy Act.

**Boundary context:**
[B.1.2 — Teams Phone under TIC 2.0 centralized DIA](../../boundary/B1-2-teams-phone-tic2-centralized-dia.html)
works this book's cloud-voice architecture against the constrained real
case — no SD-WAN, F5 removed, centralized DIA — and is the honest
counterweight to the greenfield telephony design here.

## Labs

1. Measure one-way latency, jitter, and loss to AWS us-west-2 and
   Microsoft 365 endpoints; compute the G.114 verdict for hairpin vs.
   direct paths.
2. SD-WAN policy lab: DSCP EF → lowest-latency path, HTTPS →
   highest-throughput path; verify EF markings are honored, not remarked.
3. Configure and test a Teams emergency-calling policy with LIS
   dispatchable location, documenting the 911 test.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- Migrating any office before G.114 validation — post-migration voice
  failures cost dramatically more.
- Treating DIA alone as compliance: it fixes latency but closes none of the
  flow-enforcement/monitoring controls without the SASE stack.
- Asymmetric routing misdiagnosed as "SBC misconfiguration."
- Assuming the `.com` exception is permanent — it requires re-evaluation
  each cycle; cloud SBCs need their own FedRAMP authorization.
